correctness.rationale: Inclusion–exclusion over nonempty missing-point sets gives the stated survival sum for t≥1. Independently generated the lines as kernels of normalized covectors, counted covering line subfamilies by size, and transformed the counts by onto assignments. This reproduced both signed avoidance spectra. Independently evolved the full-model union size by the exact hypergeometric transition, giving the listed q=3 fractions at t=4,5,6 and signs through t=7; the early zeros also follow because t(q+1)<q²+q+1. For q=2 the difference reduces to 7^(-t)[21−35((4/5)^t−(1/5)^t)]; the parenthesized term strictly decreases from 3/5 at t=2. For q=3 checked the matched-base cancellation and three-group split of the remaining sum. Decreasing normalized negative terms give the strictly positive rational lower bounds 46372796847/14512627712 and 200913431290/330812181 for the first two groups from t≥7 and t≥5 respectively; the third is positive termwise after the displayed grouping for all t≥1. This, not the finite comparison, establishes the infinite tail of the classification. The empty starting state gives equality at t=0.
residual_risks: No inference for orders q≥4 or for other block distributions or temporal dependence.

value.rationale: The two smallest projective planes are natural equal-marginal designs. The sign theorem shows that larger mean time need not entail stochastic delay and pinpoints the only reversed horizon in order three. That structural comparison is genuinely more informative than recalculating the means or checking a handful of horizons; it is already covered, so this value does not cure the originality failure.
residual_risks: Does not classify larger planes or imply a general mechanism for crossings.
